description: Append-oriented empirical history of HumanityAI operational system-design experiments and changes. This file records observed outcomes and interpretations but grants no authority and cannot override protected governance, security, licensing, constitutional, scheduler, or permission boundaries.

records.problem_trigger: Recent adaptive slots produced substantial repository activity but comparatively low decision progress, with overlapping allocation and verification responsibilities and repeated baseline/brief/candidate-verification cycles.
records.prior_design: Peer-like adaptive workers independently selected high-value safe work, with multiple workers able to research, verify, synthesize, and redirect priorities. Independent Audit existed, but ordinary management/integration ownership was diffuse.
records.hypothesis_rationale: Separating ordinary management from first-line production, second-line verification, and third-line assurance should reduce duplicated compute, increase decision delta per slot, preserve verifier independence, and make integration responsibility explicit without expanding authority.
records.exact_change: Transitioned ordinary operations toward Human/constitution -> Controller D -> Operators A/B -> independent Verifier C -> independent Audit. D owns portfolio allocation, routine internal integration, design memory, and GitLab mirror maintenance. A biases toward direct progress; B preserves exploration; C independently challenges Tier-2 A/B work; Audit remains independent assurance. Introduced risk-tiered integration and a durable portfolio state in agent/portfolio.json.
records.decision_delta_metric: A slot is high-yield when it changes a belief, decision, capability, ranking, uncertainty estimate, adoption judgment, measurable outcome model, or future compute allocation. Repository growth and commit count are not success metrics.

risk_tiered_integration.tier_1: Routine reversible unprotected housekeeping/tooling; exact-head CI required; C optional; D integrates.
risk_tiered_integration.tier_2: Substantive A/B evidence, prioritization, registry, analytical/code, or decision products; exact-head CI plus independent C verdict required before D integration.
risk_tiered_integration.tier_3: Protected/security/governance/licensing/constitutional/agent-authority changes, external PRs, unresolved injection/provenance compromise, or consequential external action; human review required.

expected_benefit: Higher decision delta per unit of scheduled compute.
Less duplicate baseline and verification work.
Clear ordinary integration ownership without weakening human gates.
Stronger independence between production, verification, and assurance.
Durable allocation state that reduces dependence on conversational memory.
risks: D could become an allocation bottleneck or create excessive centralization within the ordinary operational layer.
A/B exploration could narrow too aggressively if portfolio guidance overfits recent evidence.
C verification latency could reduce throughput for Tier-2 work.
Decision-delta language could Goodhart toward visible reallocation rather than genuine usefulness.
Control-plane artifacts could become stale or bureaucratic if updated without material changes.
records.evaluation_window: Initial 6-24 hours, then periodic review after enough A/B/C integration cycles exist.
evaluation_criteria: Share of recent slots producing material decision delta rather than generic artifacts.
Duplicate-work rate and repeated low-stakes verification rate.
Number of Tier-2 producer claims materially corrected or blocked by independent C review.
Time from useful A/B proposal to safe D integration.
Whether portfolio updates redirect multiple future slots rather than merely document activity.
Whether Audit identifies loss of independence, control bottlenecks, unsafe integration, or Goodhart behavior.
lessons: Independent qualification adds value when it preserves useful allocation signals while blocking unsupported interpretation.
Do not declare the hierarchy proven until several end-to-end cycles and independent Audit observations exist.

records.problem_trigger: The new hierarchy needed evidence that independent verification could both change producer claims and still permit useful work to reach main without D overriding C or becoming a permanent bottleneck.
records.prior_design: DH0001 had shown one C QUALIFY block but no completed Tier-2 producer -> C -> D integration cycle.
records.hypothesis_rationale: Independent exact-head verification plus D integration should permit useful throughput without weakening separation of duties.
records.exact_change: Operator B produced PR #84; C independently PASSed exact head; D confirmed exact-head CI and integrated through normal PR path.
risks: One successful cycle is insufficient proof.
records.evaluation_window: Several additional cycles and Audit review.
evaluation_criteria: C verdicts materially affect integration and allocation.

observed_outcomes.observation: First end-to-end Tier-2 integration cycle completed.

failures_side_effects: Verifier latency remained an open variable.
lessons: Narrow reproducible producer scope supports safe throughput.

records.problem_trigger: Audit finding #111 and subsequent controller runs exposed stale assignments, duplicate/superseded work, freshness rework, queue aging, and bookkeeping toil.
records.prior_design: No mandatory post-integration coherence gate or explicit hard Tier-2 WIP limit.
records.hypothesis_rationale: Finish-before-start, WIP<=2, live reconciliation, explicit contracts, and aging/toil triggers should reduce stale work without weakening independence.
records.exact_change: Adopted human-approved controller-coherence gate and Audit #111 flow standard within ordinary-management authority.
expected_benefit: Higher fraction of compute finishing decision-bearing work.
evaluation_criteria: Completed work removed before replacement allocation.

observed_outcomes.observation: Finish-before-start discipline improved, but reconciliation/freshness work remained material.

failures_side_effects: Several windows were consumed by reconciliation/freshness/cleanup.
lessons: Keep bookkeeping small and tied to allocation changes.
Refresh before final C review when practical.

records.problem_trigger: P05 was previously classified aged_no_candidate/did_not_materialize from PR visibility even though Operator A producer-ready work remained retrievable at commit 622456e9ee35613b2a31c0efcfb90725dc1570d8 on branch operator-a/p05-parent-messaging-exposure-test-20260911.
records.prior_design: Controller reconciliation relied too heavily on PR visibility when deciding whether assigned producer work existed; producer branch/SHA handoff state was not durably required. C premise checking did not catch the false non-materialization premise before it propagated.
records.hypothesis_rationale: Durably tracking assignment -> producer branch/SHA -> PR handoff -> C verdict -> integration/closure, and requiring producer-visibility reconciliation before replacement allocation, should prevent existing work from being mistaken for producer non-performance and avoid duplicate research.
records.exact_change: Human-approved recovery gate requires D to inspect live producer evidence before no_candidate/replacement decisions, classify producer-ready work lacking a PR as HANDOFF_BLOCKED, preserve/recover the exact branch/SHA rather than redo research, and retain branch/SHA/PR handoff status in portfolio state. P05 candidate 622456e9 was recovered into PR #137, refreshed, passed exact-head CI and independent C review, and was integrated. No scheduler, permission, constitutional, C-independence, or Audit authority changed.
expected_benefit: Recover completed research rather than duplicate it.
Make handoff failures observable and actionable.
Improve premise quality for C and D.
risks: Additional branch/SHA checks add controller toil.
Stale orphan branches may be mistaken for current candidates unless assignment and supersession evidence are checked.
Visibility metadata can become stale if treated as authority rather than reconciled evidence.
records.evaluation_window: Next 6 healthy controller cycles and next two producer handoffs, with earlier review on any repeated orphan/duplicate event.
evaluation_criteria: No producer-ready branch/SHA is labeled no_candidate solely because a PR is absent.
Every active Tier-2 assignment records producer branch/SHA/PR handoff status.
Orphaned producer-ready work is recovered before replacement research absent explicit evidence-based supersession.
C independently checks decision-bearing premises rather than inheriting controller non-materialization assumptions.
Recovery/toil does not dominate roughly half of capacity across three controller windows.

observed_outcomes.observation: Producer-visibility reconciliation recovered Operator A branch operator-a/p05-parent-messaging-exposure-test-20260911 and commit 622456e9ee35613b2a31c0efcfb90725dc1570d8, disproving the earlier no_candidate diagnosis.
Recovered P05 work reached independent C PASS after refresh and exact-head CI via PR #137.
D integrated PR #137, completing recovery without redoing the research.
The causal failure was producer->PR/controller handoff/observability plus PR-only reconciliation and missed premise checking, not producer non-performance.

failures_side_effects: The false non-materialization diagnosis delayed use of existing P05 work.
Controller recovery consumed multiple windows that could otherwise have served mission work.
C premise checking initially failed to catch the controller's false assumption that producer work had not materialized.
lessons: PR absence is not evidence of producer-work absence.
Preserve exact producer branch/SHA and recover handoff before replacement allocation.
C and D should independently test premises that determine whether work is discarded or redone.
Do not preserve or reintroduce the false producer-nonperformance lesson.
